text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Herman Franz, president of Siemens AG is visiting Romania to assess the company's local projects and meet government members.
- Agriculture ministry data show that herbicides were not used on some 1.5 million hectares, from a total of 2.4 million under wheat.
- Wheat output this year is expected to range between three to six tonnes per hectare, the newspaper says.

- RomTelecom telephone authority considers taking part in the privatisation of similar companies in neighbouring Bulgaria and Moldova -- BulgarTelecom and MolTelecom -- Communications Minister Sorin Pantis said.
- The Netherlands invested a total of $256 million in Romania to set up 751 companies, government officials said ahead of Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's visit to The Hague on Monday.

- The government drafted a law on the status of the central bank (BNR) reducing the governor's mandate to five years from eight. The bill also sets down stability of the leu currency and stability of prices as BNR main tasks.
